title: Internal Hom base change through a filtered finite-free coefficient colimit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with a sheaf of commutative rings $R$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], relative derived tensor computed using K-flat complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of sheaves of commutative $R$-algebras, with each $S_i$ isomorphic as an $R$-module sheaf to $R^{d_i}$ for a finite nonnegative integer $d_i$. Let $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ be its sheaf-algebra colimit, whose underlying module is the filtered sheaf-module colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $K\in D(R)$ satisfy the following continuity property: for every diagram $(M_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ of cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map
$$\varinjlim_i H_R(K,M_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_i M_i^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism, with filtered colimits computed by exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives. For every $L\in D(R)$ with bounded-below cohomology, the canonical evaluation-transpose comparison
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. It is natural in $K,L$ and in compatible morphisms of the algebra diagrams. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar-adjunction identification, is the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)&\simeq\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_R H_R(K,L))\\
&\simeq\varinjlim_i H_R(K,S_i\otimes_R L)\\
&\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R L).
\end{aligned}$$
In this formula a bounded-below representative of $L$ is used, and the stage comparisons are the evaluation-defined ones. They are compatible with every transition map of the diagram, independently of choices of finite bases. No constructibility of $L$ or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a complex $C$ representing $L$ and an integer $b$ such that $H^n(C)=0$ for $n<b$. Replace $C$ by $L^\bullet$ with zero terms below $b$, term $C^b/\operatorname{im}(d^{b-1})$ in degree $b$, and terms $C^n$ above $b$, with the induced differential. The quotient map $C\to L^\bullet$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at least $b$ and is an isomorphism on the zero cohomology objects below $b$. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Put $M_i^\bullet=S_i\otimes_R L^\bullet$. Every $M_i^\bullet$ vanishes termwise below the same integer $b$.

source.place: Agent argument: explicit lower good truncation, using cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms as in Tag 05RU (derived-definition-unbounded-derived-category).

proof.text: For any $R$-module sheaf $A$, tensor-colimit preservation gives $S\otimes_R A\cong\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_R A)$. The size hypothesis on the site and the smallness of $I$ are precisely those required by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. A finite basis of $S_i$ identifies $S_i\otimes_R A$ with $A^{d_i}$: the maps send $e_a\otimes x$ to the $a$-th summand and conversely. Thus tensoring with $S_i$ is exact, including $d_i=0$. Apply these exact functors to a short exact sequence and take its exact filtered colimit. The displayed tensor-colimit identification proves that $S\otimes_R-$ is exact as well. In particular, applying the same identification in every degree gives $\varinjlim_i M_i^\bullet\cong S\otimes_R L^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 03EP (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), (2); agent specialization to finite free stages, using the assumed exactness of filtered colimits.

proof.text: For $T=S_i$ or $S$, exactness of $T\otimes_R-$ implies $H^n(T\otimes_R A^\bullet)=T\otimes_R H^n(A^\bullet)$: an exact functor preserves the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology. It therefore preserves every quasi-isomorphism. Tensor a K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ with $T$. The resulting quasi-isomorphism identifies the K-flat computation of $T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ with $T\otimes_R A^\bullet$. These identifications are canonical because they are induced by the resolution maps and localization. Apply them to $A=L$ and $A=H_R(K,L)$, with no boundedness requirement on the latter. For any representative $B^\bullet$ of $H_R(K,L)$ the degreewise tensor-colimit identification also gives $S\otimes_R B^\bullet\cong\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_R B^\bullet)$. Exact filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms by the same cohomology argument, so this computes the first isomorphism of the claimed formula.

source.place: Tag 06YY (sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-base-change), identity-topos scalar extension; agent exact-functor computation.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Fix the functorial K-injective replacement $\eta_M:M\to I(M)$ of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $C=L^\bullet$ for step 1's bounded-below complex, $e=\eta_C:C\to J=I(C)$, $B=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J)$ and $F(M)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I(M))$. Thus $B$ represents $H_R(K,L)$ and $F$ is the actual functor on complexes used to represent $H_R(K,-)$. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms: naturality of $\eta$ and two-out-of-three show $I(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism whenever $u$ is; apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] to $I(u)$. For every finite $d$, $J^{\oplus d}$ is K-injective, since the component null-homotopies of a map from an acyclic complex assemble into a null-homotopy. Moreover $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J^{\oplus d})\cong B^{\oplus d}$ as complexes: $f\mapsto(\pi_a f)_a$ and $(f_a)_a\mapsto\sum_a\iota_a f_a$ are inverse, including $d=0$, and commute with the Hom differential. No lower bound on $J$ or $B$ is needed.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined); functorial replacement as in Injectives Tag 079P; agent finite-biproduct calculation.

proof.text: We will use the chain-level tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. Its degree-zero chain-map correspondence sends $\phi:A\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,E)$ to $a\otimes p\mapsto\phi(a)(p)$ on $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P)$. This formula respects the differentials: for $a$ of degree $n$, $d(\phi(a))(p)=d_E(\phi(a)(p))-(-1)^n\phi(a)(d_Pp)$. The Hom-complex isomorphism, followed by ordinary global sections and $H^0$, gives the correspondence on homotopy classes by [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy]. If $E$ is K-injective then $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,E)$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Both Hom-sets can therefore be computed in the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. For completeness, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to A$. Its acyclic cone stays acyclic after tensoring with $P$. The cone of $Q\otimes P\to A\otimes P$ is this tensor of the cone (the direct-sum terms and block differentials agree), so that map is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. The tensor descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes the derived tensor on $Q,P$; hence $A\otimes P$ computes it as well. Consequently the derived tensor-Hom transpose is computed by this chain formula, even when $A$ is not K-flat. In particular evaluation $B\otimes P\to J$ is $f\otimes p\mapsto f(p)$. The order $P\otimes B$ instead gives $p\otimes f\mapsto(-1)^{|p||f|}f(p)$ by the Koszul interchange; all uses below keep $B$ before $P$.

source.place: Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose), Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), and the chain-level construction in Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); Derived Categories Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective).

proof.text:
For every $R$-module sheaf $T$ in degree zero define actual chain maps
$$\alpha_T:T\otimes B\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,T\otimes J),\qquad \alpha_T(t\otimes f)(p)=t\otimes f(p),$$
$$a_T=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\eta_{T\otimes J})\alpha_T:T\otimes B\to F(T\otimes J),\qquad v_T=F(T\otimes e):F(T\otimes C)\to F(T\otimes J).$$
The first formula is sheaf-linear, balanced, compatible with restrictions, and hence extends through the sheaf tensor product; the Hom differential gives $d\alpha_T(t\otimes f)=\alpha_T(t\otimes df)$. For every module map $u:T\to T'$ the equality $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,u\otimes1_J)\alpha_T=\alpha_{T'}(u\otimes1_B)$ holds on $t\otimes f$, both sides sending $p$ to $u(t)\otimes f(p)$. Naturality of $\eta$ now gives the strict equalities
$$F(u\otimes1_J)a_T=a_{T'}(u\otimes1_B),\qquad F(u\otimes1_J)v_T=v_{T'}F(u\otimes1_C).$$
Thus $a_{S_i}$ and $v_{S_i}$ are transformations of actual $I$-diagrams of complexes, not merely compatible derived morphisms. The formulas also hold for $T=S$ and for the maps $S_i\to S$.

source.place: Agent chain-map and strict-naturality calculation from the Hom differential (Section 0A8X) and the functorial resolution augmentation.

proof.text:
If $T=S_i\cong R^{d_i}$, $\alpha_T$ is a chain isomorphism by step 4's projection/inclusion calculation, and $T\otimes J\cong J^{\oplus d_i}$ is K-injective. Thus $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\eta_{T\otimes J})$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], applied to a quasi-isomorphism between the K-injective complexes $T\otimes J$ and $I(T\otimes J)$. Hence $a_{S_i}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $T=S_i$ or $S$, flatness from step 2 makes $T\otimes e$ a quasi-isomorphism, and step 4 then shows $v_T$ is a quasi-isomorphism. After localization the roof
$$T\otimes B\xrightarrow{a_T}F(T\otimes J)\xleftarrow{v_T}F(T\otimes C)$$
represents the stage comparison $\beta_T=v_T^{-1}a_T$. Indeed step 5 transposes $a_T$ to $(t\otimes f)\otimes p\mapsto\eta_{T\otimes J}(t\otimes f(p))$; removing the resolution augmentation and then $T\otimes e$ gives precisely evaluation tensored with $T$. The bases were used only to prove invertibility of $a_{S_i}$; the maps and their strict transition squares were defined without bases.

source.place: Tags 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined) and 0A90 (lemma-compose); agent identification of the finite-stage roof by the chain transpose.

proof.text:
Take termwise sheaf colimits of those strict diagrams. Write $X=\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes B)\cong S\otimes B$, $W=\varinjlim_i F(S_i\otimes C)$ and $Z=\varinjlim_i F(S_i\otimes J)$. The maps $a=\varinjlim_i a_{S_i}:X\to Z$ and $v=\varinjlim_i v_{S_i}:W\to Z$ are actual chain maps and quasi-isomorphisms by steps 3 and 7. Let $\lambda_C:W\to F(S\otimes C)$ be the chain map induced by $F(S_i\otimes C\to S\otimes C)$. This is the specified continuity map on functorial representatives. The complexes $S_i\otimes C$ have the common lower bound $b$, so the hypothesis says $\lambda_C$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore, in $D(R)$,
$$\gamma=[\lambda_C][v]^{-1}[a]:S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(K,S\otimes_R L).$$
This constructs the middle arrow of the stated three-arrow formula as the colimit roof $[v]^{-1}[a]$ of strictly natural representatives of the evaluation-defined $\beta_{S_i}$. It is not obtained by taking a colimit of arbitrary derived-category maps.

source.place: Agent application of the exact termwise-colimit convention and the stated continuity hypothesis; ordinary tensor-colimit identification: Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits).

proof.text:
There is also an actual chain map $\lambda_J:Z\to F(S\otimes J)$ induced by the cocone, without assuming continuity for the possibly unbounded complex $J$. Strict naturality of $v_T$ in step 6 gives
$$\lambda_Jv=v_S\lambda_C.$$
Strict naturality of $a_T$ with respect to each $S_i\to S$ gives
$$\lambda_Ja=a_S:X=S\otimes B\to F(S\otimes J).$$
The second equality is in the category of complexes: after composition with the actual colimit injection $S_i\otimes B\to X$, the maps are $F(S_i\otimes J\to S\otimes J)a_{S_i}$ and $a_S(S_i\to S)\otimes1_B$, equal by the chain-map formula of step 6. The universal property of the colimit of complexes gives the equality before localization. These two identities imply $[v_S]\gamma=[a_S]$, and hence
$$\gamma=[v_S]^{-1}[a_S].$$
Only $v_S$ is inverted here; $\lambda_J$ need not be a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the comparison with the global evaluation map using strict chain maps, with no assertion that stage restrictions determine morphisms in $D(R)$.

source.place: Agent strict-cocone calculation. The universal property is used in complexes, before localization, not in the triangulated category.

proof.text:
Let $c$ be the stated comparison, and use the evaluation-normalized isomorphism $\theta:U H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong H_R(K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$ of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. Compose $\theta U(c)$ with $H_R(K,S\otimes e)$, represented by $v_S$. By that node's evaluation normalization its derived transpose is the scalar-extension of evaluation with $L$ represented by $J$. On the complexes of steps 4–6 this is the chain map
$$(S\otimes B)\otimes P\longrightarrow I(S\otimes J),\qquad (s\otimes f)\otimes p\longmapsto\eta_{S\otimes J}(s\otimes f(p)).$$
There is no interchange sign in regrouping $s,f,p$, since $s$ has degree zero. The differential and transpose are those of step 5. In particular this chain map is exactly the uncurrying of the already constructed $a_S$, not merely a map with the same stage restrictions. Step 5's derived adjunction bijection therefore gives $[v_S]\theta U(c)=[a_S]$. Step 9 gives the same equality for $\gamma$, so $\theta U(c)=\gamma$ after inverting $[v_S]$. Since $\gamma$ is invertible and the restriction functor $U$ is conservative by the scalar-adjunction node, $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$.

source.place: Agent identification by the chain-level transposition of Tag 0A90 and its derived realization in Tag 08J9, together with the evaluation normalization explicitly stated by the scalar-adjunction node.

proof.text: The chain adjunction in step 5 is natural in all inputs. On representatives, postcomposing $f$ by a map of $J$'s or precomposing it by a map of $P$'s commutes with $\alpha_T(t\otimes f)(p)=t\otimes f(p)$; the same is true for $a_T,v_T$ by the natural resolution augmentation. Derived internal Hom sends quasi-isomorphisms in either variable to isomorphisms, so the evaluation and transpose used in step 10 descend with this naturality to derived inputs. Together with the scalar-adjunction node's naturality, this proves that the canonical $c$ is natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $L$; its inverse is then natural whenever $c$ is invertible. For a compatible morphism of algebra diagrams, the strict equalities in step 6 hold for its maps as well, so the induced colimit maps commute with $a,v,\lambda_C$; the scalar-adjunction normalization commutes with coefficient-ring maps. Thus the same naturality holds for the formula in the statement. Boundedness was used only for the common lower bound on $S_i\otimes C$, never for $J$, $B$ or $K$.

source.place: Agent naturality check from strict chain formulas, functoriality of the Hom-complex adjunction (Tag 0A90), and the scalar-adjunction evaluation normalization.

lean.note: Universal representative formulation: P is any K-flat representative of K, L any strictly bounded-below representative of the second derived input, and E the ordinary scalar-extension functor with its specified objects and maps. Exact finite-free-colimit scalar extension computes its derived functor on these representatives. The actual map in D(S) is derivedComparison, fixed by pure-tensor evaluation and the actual localization factorization. Auxiliary declarations give its strict termwise-colimit formula, scalar-adjunction normalization and naturality. No mathematical hypothesis or clause of the node is changed.
